script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: REDEMPTION ROAD

FADE IN:

EXT. COUNTRY ROAD - DAY

A winding, picturesque country road stretches through the verdant countryside, lined with trees whose leaves rustle in the gentle breeze. The sun casts dappled light on the ground.

(NARRATOR, VO)
Everybody's got a story. Some are longer than others, some have more twists and turns, but they all begin on the same road: the road of life.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DAY

ALICE (early 40s, intelligent, wearied) sits alone at a table, nursing a cup of coffee and staring out the window at the road.

WAITRESS (late 30s, motherly, kind) places a fresh slice of pie in front of Alice.

WAITRESS
(smiling)
You look like you could use a pick-me-up. How about a slice of apple pie?

ALICE
(forcing a smile)
Thank you. I could use that.

WAITRESS
(studying Alice)
You've been coming here a lot lately. Is everything alright?

Alice hesitates before answering.

ALICE
(sighing)
No, not really. I've made some mistakes in my life, and I can't seem to escape them. I feel like I'm stuck.

WAITRESS
(nodding sympathetically)
We all make mistakes, dear. But it's never too late to make things right.

INT. ALICE'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Alice sits in her living room, surrounded by the remnants of a life she no longer recognizes. Memories flood back to her.

FLASHBACK: ALICE (younger) arguing with her husband, JACK (early 40s, cruel, manipulative) over money.

FLASHBACK: ALICE (younger) discovering Jack's affair and packing her bags.

FLASHBACK: ALICE (younger) leaving Jack and their home, tears streaming down her face.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DAY

Alice returns to the cafe, her face resolved.

WAITRESS
(surprised)
You're back again! What's new?

ALICE
(smiling)
I've decided to make a change. I'm going to find Jack and make things right between us.

WAITRESS
(concerned)
But what if he doesn't want to make things right? What if he's not changed?

ALICE
(determined)
Then I'll show him that I have. I'll be the better person.

EXT. COUNTRY ROAD - DAY

Alice sets off on her journey, her heart filled with a mixture of fear and hope.

INT. JACK'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jack sits alone in his dimly lit apartment, nursing a glass of whiskey. He hears a knock at the door.

JACK
(surprised)
Alice? What are you doing here?

ALICE
(steeling herself)
I came to talk to you. I want to make things right between us.

JACK
(laughing)
You think you can just waltz back in here and expect me to forgive you? After all the pain you caused me?

ALICE
(tearful)
I know I hurt you, Jack. I was wrong. I've been living with the guilt and the regret for years. I can't go on like this.

JACK
(sighing)
I've made my own mistakes, Alice. I've hurt people, too. But I've changed. I've learned from my mistakes.

ALICE
(hopeful)
And I have, too. I've grown, Jack. I've learned to forgive myself. And I want to forgive you, too.

Jack looks at Alice, his expression softening.

JACK
(reluctantly)
Alright. I'll try. But it's going to take time.

Alice nods, understanding.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DAY

Alice sits at her usual table, sipping her coffee and watching the road. The Waitress brings her a slice of pie.

WAITRESS
(smiling)
You look like you've made some progress.

ALICE
(smiling back)
I have. It's not easy, but it's worth it.

INT. ALICE'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Alice sits in her living room, surrounded by the memories of her past. But now, they don't bring her pain. Instead, they fill her with a sense of pride.

FLASHBACK: ALICE (older) and JACK (older) laughing together, holding hands.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DAY

Alice raises her coffee cup to the Waitress in a toast.

ALICE
(smiling)
Here's to second chances.

FADE OUT.
